details:
Many users have expressed various frustrations and concerns regarding the newly added Avatar Marketplace. After reading these posts, I decided to compile my thoughts into a post examining why this change has been so poorly received.

=== Why It Doesn't Make Sense ===

Avatar creators already have methods of monetizing their products outside of this marketplace. While it may be argued that the goal of providing this marketplace is accessibility, the fact of the matter is most people will not pay for an avatar that they cannot modify themselves. With a plethora of publicly available avatars, the main reason users buy avatars is for the ability to edit, rig, customize, and accessorize them as they please. This feature has limited, if not zero appeal to the vast majority of the player base. 

On the contrary, the success of the existing marketplace used by world creators to provide in-world benefits to their supporters serves as an example of a positive monetization strategy that adds to the user experience. The use of the marketplace for worlds provides an easier-to-use alternative to external providers like Ko-fi or Patreon, with the added benefit of being integrated into the VRChat SDK, unlike the alternative options. Functionally, it provides benefits to both the creator and their subscribers. With the avatar marketplace, using VRChat's internal system is objectively less functional and useful than the external providers already in use today, in that people who purchase avatars do not have access to the base model or files. Due to these factors, the successful monetization of worlds cannot be replicated with avatars; the Avatar Marketplace provides no benefit to the seller besides discoverability and is a net downgrade for the buyer.

=== Why It's So Unpopular == 

Regardless of the merit of the concept itself, the community is also upset at the removal of functionality caused by this update. The avatar menu now looks out of place in the current user interface and has had substantial portions of its functionality removed. Although it has been stated that this functionality will return, it begs the question: Why was this feature released in such an unfinished and unpolished state? And why was the existing avatar menu completely scrapped for a worse, uglier version that doesn't even work correctly? Similarly, the aggressive design choice of forcing users to view the marketplace every time they wish to interact with their avatars is off-putting and a hassle for people who regularly interact with their avatars. Although many non-intrusive implementations of this change were possible, the VRChat team inexplicably decided instead to obstruct the user experience and actively worsen the functionality and appearance of the avatar menu.

=== Nobody Wants This === 

Many ascribe this change to greed, but I feel that it's important to remember that one should never attribute to malice that which can be adequately explained by stupidity. With that in mind, I think the folks in charge of VRChat have fundamentally misunderstood the community's wants. This "feature" is less functional than the existing alternatives, and has actively worsened the user experience compared to the previous avatar menu.

In case the overwhelming feedback is unclear: Please keep the marketplace from obstructing the user's experience. It should be a convenience for those who wish to use it, not an inconvenience for the vast majority who will not.

=== Proposed Design ===

It would make far more sense to include the avatar marketplace in the dedicated marketplace tab already at the bottom of the menu. This would mean that all paid content is easily accessed and managed in one place.

As for the avatar menu, I question why the wheel needs to be re-invented. The previous avatar menu was very functional and easy to use. An addition of a "purchased" section for the avatar marketplace would be the only major change to the previous UI.

== Summary and Postmortem == 

Regardless of the merits of the avatar marketplace as a concept, the fact that this feature was released in such a buggy, poorly thought-out state indicates a failure in the development cycle of this game. Despite being tested and disliked in the open beta, the update was pushed through without regard for their suggestions and feedback. After being released to the general public, more complaints and frustration with these changes have come in, and despite this, the VRChat team has yet to take accountability for their actions and have consistently been deflecting the blame for things such as the loss of functionality of the avatar menu or the default homepage of the avatar tab.

Although I am frustrated with these changes, I have nothing but respect for the people who put their effort and energy into making this platform that so many of us call home. I hope that they, in turn, respect the people who make this platform such a vibrant, active community.

- _jami
title: A Letter Regarding the VRChat Avatar Marketplace
